author: Daisy Rathi
text:
You’re not imagining it nighttime readings can be especially frustrating. We were told that compression lows, sensor lag, and rapid changes can all make CGMs read much lower than a fingerstick, particularly during sleep. That doesn’t make it any easier though, especially when hypoglycemic unawareness is in the mix and you can’t just ignore a low.

What helped us wasn’t blindly trusting the number, but watching the trend and speed of change. We use Blucon Nightrider, which gives real-time readings and customizable alarms, so we can see whether it’s a steady drop, a sudden dip, or likely a false low before waking him or treating. We still confirm with fingerpricks when needed, but it’s reduced a lot of unnecessary panic and over-treating at night.

It’s such a tough balance between staying safe and not chasing every false alarm. You’re absolutely right to be cautious and you’re doing the best you can with imperfect tools. 🤍
